validity.recommendation: Correct Capacity from 350.00 MMcf/d to approximately 35 MMcf/d
validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL 10x DISCREPANCY. The sheet's Capacity (350.00 MMcf/d) matches EIA's 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' field for this docket (CP21-498) exactly, but FERC's own Federal Register notices for this project -- both the Notice of Availability of the Draft EIS (govinfo FR-2022-08-25, 2022-18332) and the Final EIS (govinfo FR-2022-12-22, 2022-27856) -- state the project 'is designed to provide about 35,000 dekatherms per day of incremental mainline capacity' (verified verbatim via pdftotext on both PDFs). 35,000 Dth/d converts to ~35 MMcf/d (1 Dth approx 1 Mcf by standard industry convention), not 350. Independently, Virginia Mercury (Dec 3 2021, archived) reports that the companion Virginia Reliability Project (P-number not this row) adds 100 MMcf/d and that the Reliability + Electrification projects TOGETHER add 135 MMcf/d -- arithmetic gives 135-100=35 MMcf/d for the Electrification Project alone, matching the FERC dekatherm figure almost exactly and confirming EIA's 350 (and the sheet's matching 350) is a 10x transcription error, most likely EIA's, inherited by the sheet. Recommend Capacity -> ~35 MMcf/d; flagging for orchestrator adjudication since it also affects the SegmentCost/Capacity-per-dollar sanity check and any downstream aggregate figures.

Existence, classification and scope confirmed independently of GEM: Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC (a TC Energy subsidiary, FERC docket CP21-498) filed and received NGA section 7 authorization (granted 2023-03-17, per FERC's Danly concurrence statement referenced in search results and the FR EIS notices) for a compressor-station-only expansion (new/replaced electric-drive units at Boswell Tavern, Goochland, and Petersburg Compressor Stations, all Virginia) -- no new pipeline segments, consistent with the sheet's LengthKnown=0/Diameter-blank convention for this row. Not a duplicate of any other roster row (distinct docket, distinct facility list, from the adjacent-but-separate 'Virginia Reliability Project', which is a ~50-mile pipe replacement south of Petersburg and is not a GEM row in this scope). Owner1 = 'Columbia Gas Transmission LLC' at 100% is accurate at the asset-holding-entity level (CGT is the sole named applicant/certificate holder for this project, no co-owners). Note for the orchestrator: the harvested citation pool (wiki_citations.json) contains a 2023 Reuters/LNG-Global report that TC Energy agreed to sell a 40% interest in the parent Columbia Gas Transmission and Columbia Gulf systems to GIC -- a corporate-parent-level equity question distinct from this project's asset ownership.
